title: Phase 3 UI Thread Isolation
description:
Phase 3 of the Interactive Job Runtime Refactor (master ticket 26/08/20/INTERACTIVE-JOB-RUNTIME-REFACTOR).

Make the UI/OS thread enqueue-only.

After this phase the UI thread may do ONLY: read and timestamp an OS event; write a fixed-size event representation into a preallocated channel; coalesce replaceable state (pointer position, wheel delta, resize, hover); atomically swap an immutable render-snapshot pointer; apply cursor, IME, accessibility and window-system directives; and submit a bounded, already-prepared rendering packet where the platform requires submission on the UI thread.

It must NOT do: domain mutation, tool logic or simulation, hit-index construction, tree reconciliation, layout, text shaping, tessellation, serialization or compression, clipboard/filesystem/network/database waits, block_on, or any arbitrary product or plugin callback.

Deliverables:
- WindowDelegate becomes an enqueue-only host contract; redraw means present the newest prepared snapshot, not build the frame.
- An immutable RenderSnapshot (scene revision, preview generation, prepared draw packets, clip and scissor state, hit-test index, cursor directive, IME directive, accessibility patch, damage regions, resource upload references), acquired atomically by the UI thread, which never waits on a worker.
- Non-interchangeable capabilities: a zero-size unforgeable UiThreadToken versus a WorkerContext. Anything that can allocate substantially, lock contended state, wait, perform I/O, mutate the document, traverse a model, run layout, create geometry or execute plugin code requires WorkerContext.
- Event interpretation, pointer registry, tool-state transitions and hit-index construction move to workers. Input generation ids prevent a late hit result from acting on stale pointer state.
- Remove the 17 pollster::block_on ParallelRuntime call sites introduced by Phase 1 packet P1e. The interactivity audit's non-allowlisted blocking bridges rose from 121 to 142 partly because of them; they run against the rule that block_on is confined to approved process and test entry points.
- Flip the forbidden-call audit from WARN to DENY for UI-reachable modules.

Design inputs already gathered in the master ticket folder as p3-design-inputs.md: only 17 of the 142 blocking bridges are UI-thread-reachable, all in the renderer glue wrapping ParallelRuntime; the hit-test QUERY is cheap enough (roughly 5-50 microseconds) to stay on the UI thread against the last committed DispatchTree while the index BUILD moves to a worker; and RenderSnapshot publication can use Arc plus AtomicPtr, mirroring the actor crate's proven SceneStore immutable-snapshot pattern.

Targets: UI event callback at most 1 ms, present callback at most 2 ms, both under the 8 ms hard ceiling, with UI callback p99 at most 2 ms.

Exit gate: thread instrumentation proves no product, plugin or domain code executes on the UI thread; no synchronous filesystem, network, clipboard or database call is reachable from it; and UI callback p99 stays at or below 2 ms in stress scenes.
